input.quote: b. paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments.
input.rationale: Section 3.4 does give Customer a convenience right on one month's notice, and IBM has no convenience right (Section 3.3 is cause-only), which matches the preferred position on notice and one-way exit. However, the right is conditioned on paying uncapped and undefined early termination charges cross-referenced to Attachment A and the Service Option Attachments, and no provision anywhere refunds prepaid Charges (search for "refund" returns nothing; Section 3.5 only accelerates Customer's payment obligations). That is a penalty-plus-no-refund exit, contrary to the preferred position of convenience termination without penalty plus pro-rata refund of prepaid fees. Redline deletes the charge condition and adds the refund; fallback is a fee capped at three months' Charges.

ops.oldText: b. paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments.
ops.newText: b. no early termination charge, penalty or other unwind fee will be payable by Customer in connection with a termination under this Section 3.4, and IBM shall refund to Customer, within thirty (30) days of the effective date of termination, any prepaid Charges for the period after the effective date of termination.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Our position is that we may exit for convenience on 30 days' notice without penalty and with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Charges, so we have removed the early termination charges in Section 3.4(b) and added the refund (the related proviso in Section 3.3 falls away accordingly). If IBM needs some recovery, we could accept a capped early termination fee of no more than three months' Charges.
proposal.summary: Remove early termination charges from Customer's convenience termination right and add pro-rata refund of prepaid Charges.
